name: Lead Green Green Tokens API
description: GPU watt-hours per million output tokens by model, GPU and configuration, with grid carbon intensity and GPU hardware reference data. Static JSON, GET only, CORS open.

endpoints.description: Sources, versions, retrieval dates, licences and this endpoint list.
The index: 32 rows, one per model and GPU, energy-optimal under the latency limit, sorted ascending.
Every model on the index with its slug, Hugging Face id, parameter counts and measured GPUs.
One model: every measured configuration (concurrency, parallelism, latency, power) and the best row per GPU.
Grid emissions intensity, gCO2e per kWh, 2024 annual average, 193 countries plus World.
Manufacturer power ceilings, memory, MIG slice profiles and one embodied-carbon figure.
AI Energy Score text-generation rows, December 2025 round: Wh per 1,000 queries at batch size 1 on H100 80GB GPUs (one card for classes A and B, several for C).
Contributed measurements accepted under the protocol, with contributor, affiliation, date, versions and MIG profile; never merged into index.json.
JSON Schema for a contributed measurement file (protocol v0.2); the build validates every submission against it.
Every change to the published data or its description: date, summary, documents, reason and source version.
The index rows as CSV, for a spreadsheet.
TypeScript types for every document, generated from the documents.
Every JSON document of the current release in one zip (the same bytes as the dated release zip).
Every dated release of api/v1, each kept unchanged at releases/<date>/ with a zip of the whole release, for citation.

sources.name: ML.ENERGY Leaderboard
sources.publisher: The ML.ENERGY Initiative (started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan)
sources.compiled_evidence: the leaderboard's public/data/index.json last_updated, and the last commit to the task files, both 2026-02-16
sources.licence: Apache-2.0 per the ml-energy/benchmark-v3 dataset card
licence_evidence: Hugging Face dataset ml-energy/benchmark-v3: tagged license:apache-2.0, ships a LICENSE file, and its dataset card's License section reads Apache-2.0
The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard web app's footer says Apache 2.0

The leaderboard repository (github.com/ml-energy/leaderboard) carries no licence file; its JSON files are reproduced here as published measurements until the ML.ENERGY team confirms that the dataset licence covers them
sources.method: Energy per output token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the steady-state window (the benchmark's steady_state_energy_per_token), measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers. Energy per request is that figure multiplied by the average output length, not a separate measurement. Prompt processing is included.
sources.selection: Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU whose median inter-token latency does not exceed 500 ms, the leaderboard's own default ceiling; no measured configuration reaches it.
sources.cite: Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark: Toward Automated Inference Energy Measurement and Optimization, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks, arXiv 2505.06371
sources.used_for: index, per-model configurations, concurrency curves, measured GPU power
sources.configurations: 328 stable configurations: the leaderboard publishes the runs that passed its stability filter; every run, including the unstable ones, is in the gated Hugging Face dataset ml-energy/benchmark-v3

sources.name: Ember, Yearly electricity data
sources.factor_basis: Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported.
sources.used_for: grid emissions intensity of total generation, gCO2e per kWh, 2024 (location-based)

caveat: GPU energy only, measured at steady state on a busy server (the most energy-efficient configuration under a latency limit). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted. Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it.
